note: 7-4 "The Way Down" slide art: Hugging Face img2img (Qwen-Image + the slothadv style model) from paste-ups of World 7's own kit and made props (tools/art/w7slide/envstarts.py, envstarts2.py), cut by tools/art/w7slide/cut.py, 2026-10-29. Not wired in yet.

chute-floor-3lane.webp.use: the chute floor, seen straight down, three lanes: grooves at x = 1/3 and 2/3; repeat it down the chute

chute-wall-roots.webp.use: chute wall: carved key-pattern stone with fig roots; repeat it along the chute

chute-wall-glyph.webp.use: chute wall variant: glyph tablets and a carved band; mix with wall-roots

chute-ceiling.webp.use: the chute ceiling seen from below: dark slabs, fig roots across them

chute-end-light.webp.use: the way out at the end of the chute: daylight and leaves seen from inside (vanishing point about x 0.5, y 0.42)

chute-far-dark.webp.use: the chute running on into torch-lit dark (vanishing point about x 0.5, y 0.42), the far view before the light shows

chamber.webp.use: side-on: the chamber he shoots out into; the chute's mouth is high on the left (its spout lip about x 0.02-0.22, y 0.70); stone floor is the bottom ~15%

obstacles.webp.anchor: ax, ay: middle of the bottom edge (where it stands on the chute floor)
obstacles.webp.use: obstacles seen from the front (from behind Pokey); lintels: duck under the slab, the posts stand at the chute sides; gap-near-lip: the floor ending before a gap; gap-far-lip: the broken front face of the floor after it; rubble-wide: jump; statue-head, rubble-pile, roots-tangle: one-lane blockers

crumble.webp.use: side-on: the hall floor giving way, frames 0-3 (whole, cracked, breaking, falling); every frame shares one box, so they line up

pokey-slide-stills.webp.satchel: strap from his left shoulder (screen left) to the bag on his right hip (screen right), checked on every still
pokey-slide-stills.webp.use: optional: Pokey from behind, repainted on model with his character model from slomatt/02 cells 1 (flipped), 10 and 14; the Hugging Face clips from them were all thrown away (see the report). Do not mirror lean-left for a right lean: a mirror puts the satchel on the wrong side.
